## 18. Bite 10 — foliation, leaf identification and accumulated trace geometry

**Recorded:** 2026-11-25  
**Lane:** ⟐ HSH_RESOURCES comparative-history lane  
**State:** FORMAL READOUT MODEL BUILT AS A COMPARISON TOOL · ◈ remains PARTIAL. The moving-film distinction from Hinton is now expressed as a family of leaves plus an explicit identification/transport of their points. Two candidate geometries are demonstrated. Neither is asserted to be the native SAT construction.

### § THE MISSING GEOMETRIC DATA

Bites 08–09 distinguish a point-valued instantaneous intersection from the curve traced by successive readouts. The latter requires more than a curve and one hypersurface. It requires:

1. an ambient manifold \(M\);
2. a one-parameter family of three-dimensional leaves \(\Sigma_\lambda\);
3. a filament/history \(\gamma\) that meets each relevant leaf once;
4. a rule identifying points on different leaves with points in a common reference three-space \(S\).

Let \(T:M\rightarrow I\) be a smooth submersion with leaves \(\Sigma_\lambda=T^{-1}(\lambda)\). Assume \(T\circ\gamma\) is monotone on the interval being studied, so the intersection point \(p_\lambda=\gamma\cap\Sigma_\lambda\) is unique. Let \(F_\lambda:S\rightarrow\Sigma_\lambda\) identify a reference three-space with the \(\lambda\)-leaf. The readout history is then

\[
q(\lambda)=F_\lambda^{-1}(p_\lambda)\in S.
\]

The instantaneous physical intersection is \(p_\lambda\), a point. The accumulated trace is the path \(q:I\rightarrow S\), which may be a circle, helix, open arc, or another curve depending on the filament, the leaves and the identification maps \(F_\lambda\).

This is the minimal formal structure needed to state what a “circular intersection trace” means without calling a sequence of points a simultaneous ring.

### ∴ CONSTRUCTION A — PARALLEL HYPERSURFACES IN FOUR-DIMENSIONAL COORDINATE SPACE

Take \(M=\mathbb R^4\), with coordinates \((x,y,z,w)\), and define parallel three-dimensional leaves

\[
\Sigma_\lambda=\{(x,y,z,w):w=\lambda\}.
\]

Use the canonical affine identification

\[
F_\lambda(x,y,z)=(x,y,z,\lambda).
\]

For an illustrative curve

\[
\gamma(s)=
\big(R\cos(ks),\ R\sin(ks),\ z_0,\ s\big),
\]

each leaf is met once at \(s=\lambda\). Therefore

\[
p_\lambda=
\big(R\cos(k\lambda),R\sin(k\lambda),z_0,\lambda\big)
\]

and

\[
q(\lambda)=
\big(R\cos(k\lambda),R\sin(k\lambda),z_0\big).
\]

The readout history is a circle of radius \(R\) in the reference three-space, even though every individual leaf intersects the one-dimensional curve at only one point.

This is a coordinate-geometric demonstration, not a native SAT equation. If \(w\) is assigned a Lorentzian time coordinate, additional metric and causal requirements apply. In the ordinary \((-+++)\) Minkowski control with \(w=ct\), this particular curve is timelike only when \((Rk)^2<1\); it is non-geodesic for \(Rk\ne0\). The Euclidean four-coordinate example and the Lorentzian physical interpretation must not be silently mixed.

### ∴ CONSTRUCTION B — CONCENTRIC THREE-SPHERE WAVEFRONTS IN POSITIVE-DEFINITE FOUR-SPACE

A different candidate begins with an origin and a radial wavefront family in Euclidean \(\mathbb R^4\):

\[
\Sigma_\rho=\{X\in\mathbb R^4:\|X\|=\rho\}
\cong S^3_\rho.
\]

Use the unit three-sphere \(S=S^3_1\) as the reference space and radial identification

\[
F_\rho(n)=\rho n,\qquad n\in S^3_1.
\]

Choose an illustrative filament/history

\[
\gamma(\rho)=\rho\,n(\rho),
\qquad
n(\rho)=
\big(\cos(k\rho),\sin(k\rho),0,0\big)\in S^3_1.
\]

Its intersection with \(\Sigma_\rho\) is the single point \(p_\rho=\gamma(\rho)\). Pulling the point back by radial projection gives

\[
q(\rho)=F_\rho^{-1}(p_\rho)=n(\rho).
\]

The readout history therefore traces a great circle in the unit \(S^3\), while the actual intersections occur one at a time on expanding, distinct \(S^3_\rho\) leaves.

This construction is geometrically compatible with a four-dimensional positive-definite radial-wavefront picture, but it does not establish that SAT uses concentric \(S^3\) wavefronts in this exact form. The archived RMS snapshot describes a three-dimensional time surface propagating outward in a four-dimensional construction; the July 3 SAT narrative separately proposes a positive-signature four-axis interpretation. The exact native metric, foliation and radial identification remain source-open.

### ∴ FINDING 1 — BOTH FLAT AND RADIAL READOUTS CAN PRODUCE A CIRCLE

The two constructions show that a circular accumulated trace does not uniquely determine the ambient geometry:

- parallel 3D leaves with affine translation can yield a circular readout;
- concentric \(S^3\) wavefronts with radial projection can also yield a circular readout.

They are not the same geometry. They differ in leaf shape, normal field, global structure, metric assumptions and natural point-identification rule. A circle in the readout therefore cannot by itself tell us whether the intended timesheet is a parallel simultaneity foliation, a radial wavefront, or another family.

### ∴ FINDING 2 — THE TRANSPORT / IDENTIFICATION RULE IS NOT OPTIONAL

The map \(F_\lambda\) is substantive data. A different \(\lambda\)-dependent identification of the same leaves changes the recorded path \(q(\lambda)\). In particular, replacing \(F_\lambda\) by \(F_\lambda\circ h_\lambda\), where \(h_\lambda:S\rightarrow S\) is a smooth family of diffeomorphisms, changes the readout coordinates to

\[
\widetilde q(\lambda)=h_\lambda^{-1}(q(\lambda)).
\]

With sufficiently flexible \(h_\lambda\), a circular readout can be made stationary in the reference coordinates, or a stationary point can be made to trace a coordinate circle. Therefore the shape of the accumulated trace is not automatically an invariant of the curve-plus-foliation pair alone.

A physical or geometrically preferred trace requires a constrained transport rule: for example, affine translation along a specified normal flow, radial projection from a specified center, or a connection/observer rule derived from the native geometry. Only after that rule is fixed can the trace's shape, winding, homotopy class or observable significance be tested.

This is not a claim that the trace is “just coordinates.” It is a statement that its invariant content has not yet been identified. A source-defined transport rule may make it geometrically meaningful.

### ∴ FINDING 3 — READOUT MOTION AND INTRINSIC FILAMENT CHANGE CAN BE SEPARATED

Hinton's distinction between the moving film reading a permanent structure and the structure itself changing can be represented by holding the leaf family and transport rule fixed while varying the curve \(\gamma\).

- **Readout contribution:** \(q(\lambda)\) changes because the same fixed higher-dimensional curve meets successive leaves at different points.
- **Intrinsic-change contribution:** a family of curves \(\gamma_\alpha\), or a time-dependent deformation of the curve within the ambient model, changes the intersection history beyond the effect of leaf progression.
- **Combined case:** both the leaf family and the filament/history vary, and the readout must record the two changes separately.

A static block-geometric curve can thus generate a nonconstant readout path without requiring the curve itself to evolve in an external time parameter. But this should not be confused with a claim that the curve has zero geometric curvature or that the resulting physical particle is unaccelerated. Those are separate metric/dynamical questions.

## Question

Does a moving family of point-valued filament intersections on a two-dimensional film or a three-dimensional timesheet carry the same braid group?

No. Under the standard configuration-space assumptions, the ambient dimension of the leaf changes the exchange group.

## Historical comparator: Hinton's two-dimensional film

In *The Fourth Dimension* (1906), chapter IV, Hinton describes a spiral crossing a moving film. At any instant the intersection is a point; the successive positions of that point trace a circle in the film. Hinton then extends the picture to multiple filamentary structures and a plane world. He explicitly calls the wider consciousness/readout hypothesis symbolic.

For multiple indistinguishable point intersections moving in a two-dimensional film without collision, the relevant unordered configuration space is the planar point-configuration space. Its fundamental group is the Artin braid group B_n. For labeled points the corresponding fundamental group is the pure braid group P_n.

Hinton's passage is therefore a useful geometrical comparator for planar braid histories, but it does not itself define an Artin braid group or claim a physical braid mechanism.

## Conditional SAT comparison: three-dimensional timesheet

The archived RMS Spacetime Filaments snapshot describes the time surface as a three-dimensional surface propagating through a four-dimensional construction. The 2026-07-03 SAT synthesis likewise treats the worldline and timesheet as primitives. The 2026-10-09 clarification describes inherited SAT as a worldline plus time wavefront, not a curve wrapped around a separate carrier.

Suppose, conditionally, that:

1. each leaf of the timesheet family is a simply connected three-manifold such as R^3 or S^3;
2. each of n distinct worldlines meets every leaf once and transversely;
3. the intersections are point-like;
4. the points are indistinguishable, remain distinct, and may move freely in all three spatial directions of the leaf;
5. collisions are excluded and the leaf-identification rule is fixed.

Then the readout is a path in the unordered configuration space C_n(M^3). For the standard M^3 = R^3 or S^3 case, its fundamental group is S_n, the permutation group. **Tock objective:** Determine what substantive changes are actually occurring in contemporary theoretical and experimental physics; understand their geometric and mathematical content; compare them carefully with SAT/H(s)H; and trace relevant historical and conceptual relationships to Hinton-era dimensional thought and modern higher-dimensional category theory.

One integrated inquiry with three distinguishable, mutually informing strands:

1. **f · Contemporary physics:** quantum gravity, quantum field theory, spacetime geometry, topology, causal/time structure, quantum information, holography, emergent spacetime, cosmology, foundations, and experimental tests.
2. **h · Historical dimensional lineage:** Hinton and other nineteenth-/early-twentieth-century higher-dimensional thought, its mathematical and physical descendants, later transformations, and documented intellectual transmission.

**ᛟ · SAT/H(s)H is the comparison and generative lens**, not a premise to be silently attributed to contemporary physics. Treat the framework's stipulated ontology as the working lens for exploration, while separately marking what is accepted physics, what is a source's proposal, what follows from SAT/H(s)H, and what remains speculative or untested.

### Central question

Is there a coherent paradigm reorganization underway in physics, or are several distinct research movements being rhetorically bundled into one? Which shifts concern physical ontology, mathematical representation, quantization, explanatory economy, or experimental access, and where do they genuinely intersect with SAT/H(s)H?

- a dated map of significant current developments and their evidential status;
- geometrical accounts of the main constructions, with dimensions and transformations explicit;
- a historical/conceptual lineage map from Hinton-era work through later mathematics and physics into higher-dimensional category theory and relatives;
- a SAT/H(s)H correspondence matrix that marks exact matches, partial analogies, differences, unresolved mappings, and potential discriminating tests;
- a concise verdict on what is shifting, what is established, what remains contested, and what the rhetoric overstates.

### Exit condition

PHY-01 closes only when the above map has been built from inspected sources, the important geometry has been reconstructed faithfully, comparisons have source-level support, uncertainty and counterexamples are visible, and a next Tock is recorded. ### 6.2 First geometrical distinctions

**Bateman–Turok model**

- The action integrates over ordinary four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime: (d^4x), with a four-derivative scalar field equation.
- The paper's auxiliary two-field formulation has an internal (O(1,1)) structure. Its two fields ((\Omega,\Upsilon)) are not two extra physical spacetime dimensions.
- The Krein state space decomposes into positive- and negative-definite sectors. This is an indefinite inner-product/state-space construction, not a spacetime embedding.
- The ghost-parity operation is a discrete symmetry of the auxiliary field formulation. The physical-process positivity argument uses the generalized Born rule and weak ghost symmetry.

**Klein-bottle cosmology**

- The bulk is explicitly six-dimensional: (M^{3,1}\times K^2), namely four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime times a two-dimensional compact Klein bottle.
- The Klein bottle can be constructed from a covering torus/rectangle with identifications of the form
  [
  (x^4,x^5)\sim(x^4+2\pi r_4,x^5),\qquad
  (x^4,x^5)\sim(-x^4,x^5+2\pi r_5).
  ]
- The twist reverses one internal coordinate under traversal of the other. The resulting compact surface is non-orientable; the local geometry is flat while global topology changes the allowed field/boundary structure.
- A 3+1-dimensional brane is embedded in the 5+1-dimensional bulk. The paper studies what happens when it moves through condensate walls associated with the Klein-bottle topology.

Do not merge these models: the first has an auxiliary indefinite field/state-space structure within 4D spacetime; the second has a genuinely higher-dimensional physical spacetime with a compact non-orientable internal surface.

The paper calls its result a modest step, focuses on short-distance perturbative scattering, establishes tree-level positivity, and explicitly leaves massless collinear infrared divergences and their regulation/resummation as further work. Its conformally flat quadratic-gravity limit decouples spin-two graviton modes.

## 7. Bite 02 — Hinton, slicing geometry, and the actual categorical route into physics

**Recorded:** 2026-11-25T05:33:59.584Z  
**State:** Primary Hinton excerpts inspected; category/history and mathematical-physics bridges inspected from external primary/research literature; internal archive search remains pending. This is a bounded historical/geometric comparison, not a complete genealogy.

### 7.1 Hinton primary sources: what the texts actually say

**Charles Howard Hinton, *The Fourth Dimension* (1904 first edition; archived text is the 1906 second edition):**

- In the chapter passage around archived text lines 990–1044, Hinton constructs a plane-world analogy: a static spiral intersects a moving plane/film; successive intersections appear as a moving point. He then extends the construction to complicated structures made of filaments, whose intersections with the film are proposed as the “atoms” of the lower-dimensional world. The plane's steady traversal produces a time-series of changing cross-sections, while the higher-dimensional structure is conceived as comparatively permanent.
- This is an explicit historical example of persistent higher-dimensional structures generating lower-dimensional traces and apparent motion through a moving section. Its explanatory frame includes a plane of consciousness and philosophical readings of Parmenides; it is not a Lorentzian spacetime model, an experimentally established account of matter, or a derivation of quantum physics.
- In the later vortex passage (archived lines 2880–2925), Hinton generalizes a 3D vortex filament to a 4D vortex-sheet construction with a planar axis. He speculates about an analogy to electric current and field. Preserve this as Hinton's historical proposal, not as a correct account of electromagnetism.

**Hinton, *A New Era of Thought* (1888):**

- The source is a constructive programme for conceiving four-dimensional figures through lower-dimensional sections, projections, models, and constrained reasoning by a hypothetical plane-being.
- The tessaract exercises stress deriving the possible sections from measured relations and projections, rather than treating four-dimensional geometry as unconstrained imagination. The text explicitly says the value is in the process of determining the sections, not simply viewing pre-drawn shapes.
- The source's geometric method is a major historical lead for our visualization practice. It is not the same as the 1906 filament/film passage, and the two texts should retain separate source anchors.

### 7.3 The historical route into category theory is different

The primary chronology supported by the inspected history is not a straight line from Hinton to higher categories:

1. **19th-century higher-dimensional geometry:** Riemann, Schläfli and other mathematicians develop abstract geometries and higher-dimensional figures. Hinton's work is one important popular, pedagogical and speculative strand that trains intuition through projection, sectioning and models.
2. **Algebraic topology / homological algebra:** homology and cohomology create a need to compare spaces, groups and algebraic invariants in a systematic way.
3. **Eilenberg and Mac Lane (1945):** category theory is introduced to organize functors and natural transformations, especially the relation between algebraic and topological structures. It is not introduced as a theory of extra spatial dimensions.
4. **Grothendieck, Lawvere and later developments:** categories become intrinsic mathematical environments; homotopy theory, groupoids and the “category of categories” lead to higher categories and weak (n)-categorical structures.
5. **Higher categories in physics:** Atiyah-style TQFT assigns algebraic data to manifolds and bordisms. Baez and Dolan (1995) develop the programme of (n)-dimensional TQFTs as representations of (n)-categories. Here (k)-morphisms can be represented by (k)-dimensional manifolds, including boundaries and corners. This is a concrete bridge between geometric dimension and categorical composition, not proof that categorical degrees are additional physical spatial dimensions.

**Genealogical conclusion:** Hinton's higher-space programme and category theory are historically adjacent/convergent strands that meet in modern geometry and mathematical physics, but the inspected sources do not establish direct Hinton → Eilenberg/Mac Lane → higher category transmission. Do not claim that Hinton founded or directly caused category theory.

### 7.4 Concrete mathematical-physics bridges

**Extended TQFT / bordism:** Baez & Dolan, *Higher-Dimensional Algebra and Topological Quantum Field Theory* (1995), explicitly propose higher categories to encode extended local structure in TQFT. The geometric hierarchy is point → 1-dimensional bordism → 2-dimensional bordism between bordisms → higher-dimensional morphisms. The categorical hierarchy organises how local pieces compose and glue.

**Higher gauge theory / topological matter:** Delcamp & Tiwari, *On 2-form gauge models of topological phases* (JHEP, 2019), study 2-form topological gauge theories in 3+1 dimensions. Their construction uses the second classifying space (B^2G), 2-form cocycles and a relation between 2-form 4-cocycles, associators and braiding isomorphisms in a premodular category, with a connection to the Walker-Wang model. This is a concrete case where higher gauge fields, homotopy, categorical braiding and physical topological phases meet.

**Current 2026 higher-gauge programme:** Hisham Sati & Urs Schreiber, *Complete Topological Quantization of Higher Gauge Fields* (dated 3 June 2026; expanded lecture notes), develops global completion and topological quantization of higher gauge fields appearing in higher-dimensional supergravity. It uses differential forms of multiple degrees, (L_infty)-algebras, smooth (infty)-groupoids, nonabelian differential cohomology, cohomotopy and phase-space stacks. The authors distinguish a 5D Maxwell-Chern-Simons example (Hypothesis (h), 2-cohomotopy) from an analogous 11D C-field completion (Hypothesis (H), 4-cohomotopy) associated with the conjectural M-theory topological sector and M5-branes. These are the authors' named research hypotheses/programme, not settled consensus physics. Their “Hypothesis H” is only a naming coincidence with H(s)H; no relation or influence is assumed.

**Dimensional discipline:** differential-form degree, homotopy degree, categorical morphism level, brane dimension, compactification dimension and physical spacetime dimension are related in specific constructions but are not interchangeable. A 2-form field, a 2-morphism and a 2-dimensional surface are not automatically the same object.

### ∴ FINDING 1 — THE FILM/FILAMENT MODEL IS A SYMBOLIC PHILOSOPHICAL ANALOGY

In *The Fourth Dimension*, Hinton uses a static spiral traversed by a moving film. The successive intersections appear to an observer associated with the film as a moving point. He extends the illustration to complicated filamentary structures whose intersections could appear as the atoms and moving bodies of a lower-dimensional world.

The passage is explicitly framed as a representation of Parmenides' contrast between permanent being and apparent change. It explores a possible relation between a complete higher-dimensional existence and a temporally successive lower-dimensional experience. Hinton then considers a modified case in which the higher structure itself changes while the film traverses it, producing two sources of apparent motion.

### ∴ A NEW ERA PART I — THEORY, PRACTICE AND THE SELF-ELEMENTS OF KNOWLEDGE

The 1888 *A New Era of Thought* copy contains two especially relevant Part I discussions, within the portion the editors say is printed almost exactly as Hinton wrote it:

1. **Chapter IV, “Theory and Practice” (book pages 24–28; repository text around line 1088):** Hinton argues that scientific knowledge is not exhausted by intellectual acquaintance with principles; it includes being able to act in accordance with facts through practical manipulation. He extends the distinction to moral life: abstract knowledge of justice is different from the practical ability to act justly. His examples connect learning chemistry, manipulating material apparatus, changing one's point of view, forming habits and developing an emotional response to justice and the lives of others.
2. **Chapter V, “Knowledge: Self-Elements” (book pages 29–34; repository text around line 1229):** Hinton uses a named 3×3×3 block of twenty-seven cubes to examine how a learner's spatial knowledge incorporates the observer's conditions. The familiar above/below relation is treated as a “self element” because it is strongly shaped by gravity and the observer's habitual orientation. He proposes repeatedly changing which cubes are mentally central, and otherwise reorganizing the representation, to reduce the dominance of that observer-conditioned feature.

These passages show Hinton's dimensional programme intersecting with **epistemology, pedagogy, practical science, embodied/model-based learning and moral philosophy**. The geometry is not merely an illustration added to an otherwise independent philosophy: Hinton is using disciplined spatial reconstruction as a way to investigate how knowledge is acquired, how observer-conditioned assumptions enter representation, and how practice transforms understanding.

**Limits:** this is Hinton's philosophical and pedagogical argument, not a modern cognitive-science experiment, a derivation of relativistic frame invariance, a quantum observer effect, or an established moral theory. The comparison with contemporary ideas of situated or embodied cognition remains a historical/comparative question, not an attribution of influence.

### ⋈ INTERDISCIPLINARY MAP — NOW MORE PRECISE

- **Mathematics ↔ epistemology:** the two-way ordering scheme in *The Fourth Dimension* distinguishes order from metric distance; the cube-block exercise in *A New Era* examines observer-conditioned spatial relations. These are different arguments and should remain separate.
- **Geometry ↔ pedagogy/material practice:** Hinton's own Part I argues that spatial knowledge must be built through manipulation and sustained familiarity, not merely through verbal rules or passive viewing. The detailed Appendix H tessaract exercises are later/editor-authored elaborations.
- **Science ↔ moral philosophy:** *A New Era* Chapter IV explicitly compares theoretical/practical knowledge in chemistry and moral action, then relates the development of habits and perspective-taking to justice and altruism. Record this as Hinton's philosophical programme, not as an empirical result.
- **Fluid mechanics ↔ electromagnetism:** the 4D vortex/ether-current proposal in *The Fourth Dimension* remains a distinct historical physical conjecture requiring its own lineage.
- **Dimensional geometry ↔ philosophical time:** the film/filament readout analogy remains symbolic by Hinton's own qualification, not his validated physical account of time.

## 17. Bite 09 — Hinton's moving-film geometry and the meaning of a circular trace

**Recorded:** 2026-11-25  
**Lane:** ⟐ HSH_RESOURCES comparative-history lane

### § PRIMARY SOURCE

Charles Howard Hinton, *The Fourth Dimension*, 1906 Swan Sonnenschein edition, chapter IV, “The First Chapter in the History of Four Space.” HSH_RESOURCES transcription blob ece2e416bbc417d79a98b9ae90ec385361d85ae3; exact passage begins around repository line 989, with the spiral/film statement at line 1004, filamentary structures at line 1018, the plane-world generalization at line 1030, and Hinton's explicit “merely symbolical” qualification at line 1097. The repository transcription is derived from Internet Archive page images and omits illustrations; the title-page metadata identifies the 1906 edition.

### ∴ FINDING 1 — INSTANTANEOUS INTERSECTION AND RECORDED TRAJECTORY ARE DIFFERENT OBJECTS

Hinton's concrete analogy begins with a slanted stick intersecting a still-water surface. At any instant, the stick and water meet at a point; as the stick moves, the point moves. He then replaces the water with a thin film and introduces a spiral passing through it. The instantaneous intersection remains a point, while the successive positions of that point trace a circle in the film's own readout.

The geometry can be separated as follows:

1. **Ambient construction:** a spiral curve is embedded in a higher-dimensional setting.
2. **Instantaneous cut:** a moving film intersects the spiral at a point.
3. **Readout history:** as the film advances, the intersection point is recorded at successive internal film-coordinates.
4. **Displayed trace:** the ordered locus of those successive coordinates is circular.

The circle is therefore not the instantaneous curve–film intersection. It is the trajectory/locus of the point-valued intersections under the advancing family of films and the chosen coordinates of the film observer.

This is consistent with the dimension rule in Bite 08: a transverse 1D curve meeting a 2D film in a 3D analogy, or a 1D worldline meeting a 3D hypersurface in 4D, generically gives a 0D intersection at each instant. A one-dimensional path can arise from the succession of those point intersections.

### ∴ FINDING 2 — HINTON ALSO SEPARATES SECTION-MOTION FROM INTRINSIC CHANGE

Hinton then asks what happens if the higher-dimensional filamentary structures themselves move while the film traverses them. He distinguishes two contributions to the lower-dimensional observer's apparent motion:

- the motion produced by the advancing film reading off a structure that is otherwise permanent;
- additional motion produced by changes in the higher-dimensional structure during the traversal.

This is a precise historical distinction between **readout-induced apparent motion** and **intrinsic change of the object being read**. It is conceptually useful when comparing a propagating timesheet with a filament/worldline whose own geometry may also vary. The two contributions should be represented separately rather than bundled into a single undifferentiated “motion” term.

### ∴ FINDING 3 — THE HISTORICAL LIMIT IS PART OF THE MODEL

Hinton generalizes from the plane-world analogy to a higher-dimensional existence traversed by a “space of consciousness.” He explicitly cautions that, as far as he can see, this representation is **merely symbolical**, and that the true route to investigating higher dimensionality lies elsewhere.

Accordingly, the model is evidence about Hinton's philosophical and geometrical imagination, not a derivation of physical time, a Lorentzian foliation, a causal law, or a verified higher-dimensional physical mechanism. Its value here is the clean distinction between instantaneous section and accumulated readout history, together with Hinton's own warning not to literalize the analogy.

## 18. Bite 10 — foliation, leaf identification and accumulated trace geometry

**Recorded:** 2026-11-25  
**Lane:** ⟐ HSH_RESOURCES comparative-history lane  
**State:** FORMAL READOUT MODEL BUILT AS A COMPARISON TOOL · ◈ remains PARTIAL. ### § THE MISSING GEOMETRIC DATA

Bites 08–09 distinguish a point-valued instantaneous intersection from the curve traced by successive readouts. The latter requires more than a curve and one hypersurface. It requires:

1. an ambient manifold \(M\);
2. a one-parameter family of three-dimensional leaves \(\Sigma_\lambda\);
3. a filament/history \(\gamma\) that meets each relevant leaf once;
4. a rule identifying points on different leaves with points in a common reference three-space \(S\).

Let \(T:M\rightarrow I\) be a smooth submersion with leaves \(\Sigma_\lambda=T^{-1}(\lambda)\). Assume \(T\circ\gamma\) is monotone on the interval being studied, so the intersection point \(p_\lambda=\gamma\cap\Sigma_\lambda\) is unique. Let \(F_\lambda:S\rightarrow\Sigma_\lambda\) identify a reference three-space with the \(\lambda\)-leaf. The readout history is then

\[
q(\lambda)=F_\lambda^{-1}(p_\lambda)\in S.
\]

The instantaneous physical intersection is \(p_\lambda\), a point. The accumulated trace is the path \(q:I\rightarrow S\), which may be a circle, helix, open arc, or another curve depending on the filament, the leaves and the identification maps \(F_\lambda\).

This is the minimal formal structure needed to state what a “circular intersection trace” means without calling a sequence of points a simultaneous ring.

### ∴ CONSTRUCTION A — PARALLEL HYPERSURFACES IN FOUR-DIMENSIONAL COORDINATE SPACE

Take \(M=\mathbb R^4\), with coordinates \((x,y,z,w)\), and define parallel three-dimensional leaves

\[
\Sigma_\lambda=\{(x,y,z,w):w=\lambda\}.
\]

Use the canonical affine identification

\[
F_\lambda(x,y,z)=(x,y,z,\lambda).
\]

For an illustrative curve

\[
\gamma(s)=
\big(R\cos(ks),\ R\sin(ks),\ z_0,\ s\big),
\]

each leaf is met once at \(s=\lambda\). Therefore

\[
p_\lambda=
\big(R\cos(k\lambda),R\sin(k\lambda),z_0,\lambda\big)
\]

and

\[
q(\lambda)=
\big(R\cos(k\lambda),R\sin(k\lambda),z_0\big).
\]

The readout history is a circle of radius \(R\) in the reference three-space, even though every individual leaf intersects the one-dimensional curve at only one point.

This is a coordinate-geometric demonstration, not a native SAT equation. If \(w\) is assigned a Lorentzian time coordinate, additional metric and causal requirements apply. In the ordinary \((-+++)\) Minkowski control with \(w=ct\), this particular curve is timelike only when \((Rk)^2<1\); it is non-geodesic for \(Rk\ne0\). The Euclidean four-coordinate example and the Lorentzian physical interpretation must not be silently mixed.

### ∴ CONSTRUCTION B — CONCENTRIC THREE-SPHERE WAVEFRONTS IN POSITIVE-DEFINITE FOUR-SPACE

A different candidate begins with an origin and a radial wavefront family in Euclidean \(\mathbb R^4\):

\[
\Sigma_\rho=\{X\in\mathbb R^4:\|X\|=\rho\}
\cong S^3_\rho.
\]

Use the unit three-sphere \(S=S^3_1\) as the reference space and radial identification

\[
F_\rho(n)=\rho n,\qquad n\in S^3_1.
\]

Choose an illustrative filament/history

\[
\gamma(\rho)=\rho\,n(\rho),
\qquad
n(\rho)=
\big(\cos(k\rho),\sin(k\rho),0,0\big)\in S^3_1.
\]

Its intersection with \(\Sigma_\rho\) is the single point \(p_\rho=\gamma(\rho)\). Pulling the point back by radial projection gives

\[
q(\rho)=F_\rho^{-1}(p_\rho)=n(\rho).
\]

The readout history therefore traces a great circle in the unit \(S^3\), while the actual intersections occur one at a time on expanding, distinct \(S^3_\rho\) leaves.

This construction is geometrically compatible with a four-dimensional positive-definite radial-wavefront picture, but it does not establish that SAT uses concentric \(S^3\) wavefronts in this exact form. The archived RMS snapshot describes a three-dimensional time surface propagating outward in a four-dimensional construction; the July 3 SAT narrative separately proposes a positive-signature four-axis interpretation. The exact native metric, foliation and radial identification remain source-open.

### ∴ FINDING 1 — BOTH FLAT AND RADIAL READOUTS CAN PRODUCE A CIRCLE

The two constructions show that a circular accumulated trace does not uniquely determine the ambient geometry:

- parallel 3D leaves with affine translation can yield a circular readout;
- concentric \(S^3\) wavefronts with radial projection can also yield a circular readout.

They are not the same geometry. They differ in leaf shape, normal field, global structure, metric assumptions and natural point-identification rule. A circle in the readout therefore cannot by itself tell us whether the intended timesheet is a parallel simultaneity foliation, a radial wavefront, or another family.

### ∴ FINDING 2 — THE TRANSPORT / IDENTIFICATION RULE IS NOT OPTIONAL

The map \(F_\lambda\) is substantive data. A different \(\lambda\)-dependent identification of the same leaves changes the recorded path \(q(\lambda)\). In particular, replacing \(F_\lambda\) by \(F_\lambda\circ h_\lambda\), where \(h_\lambda:S\rightarrow S\) is a smooth family of diffeomorphisms, changes the readout coordinates to

\[
\widetilde q(\lambda)=h_\lambda^{-1}(q(\lambda)).
\]

With sufficiently flexible \(h_\lambda\), a circular readout can be made stationary in the reference coordinates, or a stationary point can be made to trace a coordinate circle. Therefore the shape of the accumulated trace is not automatically an invariant of the curve-plus-foliation pair alone.

A physical or geometrically preferred trace requires a constrained transport rule: for example, affine translation along a specified normal flow, radial projection from a specified center, or a connection/observer rule derived from the native geometry. Only after that rule is fixed can the trace's shape, winding, homotopy class or observable significance be tested.

This is not a claim that the trace is “just coordinates.” It is a statement that its invariant content has not yet been identified. A source-defined transport rule may make it geometrically meaningful.

### ∴ FINDING 3 — READOUT MOTION AND INTRINSIC FILAMENT CHANGE CAN BE SEPARATED

Hinton's distinction between the moving film reading a permanent structure and the structure itself changing can be represented by holding the leaf family and transport rule fixed while varying the curve \(\gamma\).

- **Readout contribution:** \(q(\lambda)\) changes because the same fixed higher-dimensional curve meets successive leaves at different points.
- **Intrinsic-change contribution:** a family of curves \(\gamma_\alpha\), or a time-dependent deformation of the curve within the ambient model, changes the intersection history beyond the effect of leaf progression.
- **Combined case:** both the leaf family and the filament/history vary, and the readout must record the two changes separately.

A static block-geometric curve can thus generate a nonconstant readout path without requiring the curve itself to evolve in an external time parameter. But this should not be confused with a claim that the curve has zero geometric curvature or that the resulting physical particle is unaccelerated. Those are separate metric/dynamical questions.

Hinton's 1906 comparator uses a two-dimensional film. Multiple point-valued intersections moving on that film, if they remain distinct and indistinguishable, are governed by the planar configuration space and can carry Artin braid classes. Hinton's text itself describes the successive path of a point intersection; it does not define the braid group or propose a physical braid mechanism.

The archived SAT/RMS description instead calls the timesheet a three-dimensional surface in a four-dimensional construction. If n point-valued filament intersections move freely across a simply connected three-dimensional leaf, under standard point-particle and collision-exclusion assumptions, the unordered configuration-space fundamental group is S_n, not the planar Artin braid group B_n.

### ∴ TWO-POINT CHECK

For two ordered points in R^d, the configuration space is R^d × (R^d minus the origin), which deformation-retracts to S^(d-1). Thus:

- In d=2, π1(S^1)=Z. The ordered case gives P₂; the unordered case gives B₂, also isomorphic to Z. A half-turn of the relative vector exchanges the two points; a full turn corresponds to the pure-braid subgroup.
- In d=3, π1(S^2)=0 for the ordered case. The unordered quotient has relative directions identified antipodally, giving RP² with π1=Z₂, isomorphic to S₂. Standard point-particle exchange retains parity, not an unrestricted integer winding.

This is the reason a projected crossing diagram cannot by itself establish an Artin braid on a three-dimensional timesheet.

### 1. The plan now has a dedicated braid stage

I registered **ℬ (U+212C)** in the HSH_RESOURCES code ledger, with this sequence:

\[
\boxed{\ ◈\ \longrightarrow\ \mathcal B\ \longrightarrow\ \partial\ \longrightarrow\ \Delta\ }
\]

That means: establish the actual objects and core geometry; investigate braid theory and motion groups; define composable histories; then test projection fidelity.

The dedicated plan covers classical and pure braid groups, configuration spaces, extended-object motion groups, loop braids, braided categories, Yang–Baxter structures, topological field theory, and their historical and physical connections.

[Read the dedicated braid-theory research plan](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/WORKSPACES/PHYSICS/PHY01_BRAID_THEORY_RESEARCH_PLAN_20261125.md)

### 2. A useful distinction emerged from the internal source history

The existing SAT/H(s)H material uses braiding in at least three different ways:

| Meaning | What it describes |
|---|---|
| Internal composite encoding | Braided constituent strands proposed for quarks and mesons |
| Inter-worldtube interaction | Interbraid/back-tug between distinct, interlocked worldtube histories |
| Cumulative winding | An unwrapped count of relative turns through a history |

These are different mathematical problems. In particular, a triple-braid composite is not automatically an exchange braid among three particles. And a cumulative turn count is not automatically a braid-group element.

[Read the internal braid-source stratigraphy](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/WORKSPACES/PHYSICS/PHY01_BRAID_SOURCE_STRATIGRAPHY_20261125.md)

### 3. The first dimensional discriminator

There is an especially interesting connection between Hinton's moving-film analogy and the SAT timesheet.

Under standard point-particle assumptions:

- A two-dimensional film supports planar point braids, with exchange group \(B_n\).
- A three-dimensional timesheet with freely moving point intersections instead gives the permutation group \(S_n\).

For two points, the contrast is particularly clear:

\[
B_2\cong\mathbb Z,\qquad S_2\cong\mathbb Z_2.
\]

So a richer braid structure on a three-dimensional timesheet would need something additional: a genuine two-dimensional constraint, extended intersection objects, nontrivial spatial topology, or another explicitly defined embedding/motion structure.

This is conditional mathematics, not a verdict about SAT. The actual timesheet and finite-core geometry still need to be recovered.

[Read the dimensional-uplift analysis](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/WORKSPACES/PHYSICS/PHY01_BRAID_DIMENSIONAL_UPLIFT_20261125.md)

### 4. Repository and execution status

The research plan, source stratigraphy and new dimensional analysis are committed to HSH_RESOURCES. The main PHYS-01 ledger now records Bites 11–13.

Doesn't have to be PHYS only. The way I see it, braid theory is the meticulous application of the same principles SAT/H(s)H independently converged on from its Minkowski roots, to specific particle systems and abstractified beyond lay understanding to escape spiritualist associations, then evolved and diffused throughout especially particle physics, but more broadly into cosmology and quantum computing and other fields as well. It's that lens we want to use to investigate nLab/n-Category Cafe (because they're the closest I've found to folks in the sciences who still have an almost Hintonian view, kind of explicitly). It's just that SAT took a different methodological path, using Minkowski sufficientism and extreme economy of primitives, using geometry as the way to isolate our universe from the vast landscape that the multiplicity of higher category theory and its descendants created; rather than to look at *all* relationships between *all* relationships, we said: Let's just pick the simplest one and see how far it gets us. You can see how far it's gotten us. You and I rebuilt a hundred years of physics in a year, through a different lens (with the benefit of a hundred years of mathematical and experimental physics behind us). Eg, "What if Minkowski's simplicity...but with all the data?" The answer turned out to be: "Basically, Hinton." Now, we're investigating how thoroughly these lines of thinking have shaped the last hundred years of physics, and the last two years through that lens. The answer, tentatively, seems to be: "Foundationally, thoroughly, and continually. And in some quarters, self-awarely." 

So, let's continue.

The object of study is the migration and transformation of a geometric way of thinking: higher-dimensional structure, lower-dimensional readout, constrained relations and histories of interaction. I’ll trace what is documented across mathematics, particle physics, cosmology and quantum computing, while keeping direct influence, independent convergence and retrospective resemblance separate.

I think the stronger framing is this: **we are investigating a recurring geometric research programme, not merely the history of braid groups.**

The programme has a recognizable sequence:

1. Start with entities and their geometrical relations.
2. Represent interactions as paths, crossings, junctions, compositions or deformations.
3. Identify which transformations preserve the meaningful structure.
4. Abstract those constraints into algebraic or categorical machinery.
5. Carry that machinery into new domains, sometimes far removed from its original geometric intuition.
6. Ask whether the abstraction still captures the constraints of the physical system, or whether it has acquired freedoms the physical system never possessed.

That is a much broader inquiry than PHYS-01. Braid theory becomes one particularly revealing case because its geometric origins, algebraic abstraction and later applications remain unusually visible.

And there is already evidence for the self-aware part of your hypothesis: John Baez and Aaron Lauda's *A Prehistory of n-Categorical Physics* explicitly traces how categorical ideas entered physics, including the development of monoidal and braided monoidal categories alongside developments in quantum and field theory. They describe their account as one subjective historical reconstruction, not the definitive genealogy. <Cite refs={["turn753855view4"]}/>

- **2026-07-03 SAT narrative:** braiding is introduced as a chosen representational leap to encode color confinement and composite-particle structure. The source explicitly calls it a leap and later refers to geometric leaps / representational choices.
- **2026-10-09 clarification:** the inherited SAT primitive remains a worldline plus time wavefront, not a curve wrapped around an independent carrier. H(s)H adds a separate tentative finite-core worldtube. The Kerr ring is a possible intersectional trace.
- **2026-10-17 BR-006:** Interbraid is stated more strongly as a framework-internal geometric interaction constraint among complete worldtube histories; an unwrapped cumulative-turn expression is recorded.

This is a change in emphasis from a compositional representation toward a proposed worldtube-interaction mechanism. It is not a derivation from Artin braid theory, a proof of a motion group, a quantum-statistical exchange representation or experimental confirmation.

## The dimensional turn-count discriminator

A scalar turn counter may map to a winding number only after its configuration space is specified.

- Two ordered points in a plane have a relative-position vector in the punctured plane; its loops have an integer winding class.
- For two unordered points in a plane, exchange generates the two-strand Artin braid group, isomorphic to the integers. A full 2 pi rotation of a chosen ordered relative vector corresponds to the pure-braid subgroup, not automatically to a single exchange generator.
- For two indistinguishable point particles in ordinary three-space, the standard unordered configuration-space fundamental group is S2, recording exchange parity rather than an unrestricted integer winding history.
- Extended loops/rings in three-space require their own motion/embedding group. Neither the planar Artin braid model nor the point-particle permutation model can be assumed.

Thus the BR-006 integer might map to a winding or pure-braid class in a specifically defined planar two-object model, and its parity might map to an exchange class in a standard three-dimensional point-particle model. Neither mapping follows from the formula alone. Relative angle, lift, endpoints, labels, collisions, spatial dimension and allowed homotopies must be specified.

This is a mathematical discriminator for ℬ, not an assignment of planar or three-dimensional statistics to H(s)H.

A triple-braid internal structure asks how constituent strands are embedded and constrained to form one composite object. An exchange braid asks how several distinguishable or indistinguishable objects move in a configuration space. The inputs differ:

- Internal composite: identify strands, ambient embedding, endpoints/closures and equivalence of internal configurations.
- Exchange/motion: identify objects exchanged, spatial configuration space, labels or quotient-by-permutation, excluded collisions and allowed loops/homotopies.

A Borromean- or Hopf-like section could be a readout of a higher-dimensional composite, but requires an explicit source-defined projection and invariant comparison. A familiar drawing does not establish the higher-dimensional embedding or physical identity.

1. Recover ◈: actual filament, timesheet family, transport rule, finite-core cross-section and boundaries.

6. Connect to ∂ and Δ after boundaries/composition and projection maps are explicit.

## 1. Tock: PHY-01 — Contemporary physics and the higher-dimensional synthesis

**State:** ACTIVE  
**Tock objective:** Determine what substantive changes are actually occurring in contemporary theoretical and experimental physics; understand their geometric and mathematical content; compare them carefully with SAT/H(s)H; and trace relevant historical and conceptual relationships to Hinton-era dimensional thought and modern higher-dimensional category theory.

### Scope

One integrated inquiry with three distinguishable, mutually informing strands:

1. **f · Contemporary physics:** quantum gravity, quantum field theory, spacetime geometry, topology, causal/time structure, quantum information, holography, emergent spacetime, cosmology, foundations, and experimental tests.
2. **h · Historical dimensional lineage:** Hinton and other nineteenth-/early-twentieth-century higher-dimensional thought, its mathematical and physical descendants, later transformations, and documented intellectual transmission.
3. **k · Higher-dimensional mathematics:** category theory, higher categories, higher-dimensional morphisms, homotopy theory, groupoids, braids, topological field theory, higher gauge theory, and neighboring structures, read geometrically.

**ᛟ · SAT/H(s)H is the comparison and generative lens**, not a premise to be silently attributed to contemporary physics. Treat the framework's stipulated ontology as the working lens for exploration, while separately marking what is accepted physics, what is a source's proposal, what follows from SAT/H(s)H, and what remains speculative or untested.

### Central question

Is there a coherent paradigm reorganization underway in physics, or are several distinct research movements being rhetorically bundled into one? Which shifts concern physical ontology, mathematical representation, quantization, explanatory economy, or experimental access, and where do they genuinely intersect with SAT/H(s)H?

### Deliverable

A source-grounded geometric atlas and comparison map containing:

- a dated map of significant current developments and their evidential status;
- geometrical accounts of the main constructions, with dimensions and transformations explicit;
- a historical/conceptual lineage map from Hinton-era work through later mathematics and physics into higher-dimensional category theory and relatives;
- a SAT/H(s)H correspondence matrix that marks exact matches, partial analogies, differences, unresolved mappings, and potential discriminating tests;
- a concise verdict on what is shifting, what is established, what remains contested, and what the rhetoric overstates.

### Exit condition

PHY-01 closes only when the above map has been built from inspected sources, the important geometry has been reconstructed faithfully, comparisons have source-level support, uncertainty and counterexamples are visible, and a next Tock is recorded. The Tock does **not** require proving SAT/H(s)H or declaring a new mainstream consensus.

## 3. Credenza

The Credenza is the working cabinet for Tocks: it routes active work, preserves context and re-entry conditions, and keeps useful possibilities visible without forcing them into the current bite. > **Small but significant bites. Don't choke, don't nibble.**

**Status:** Bespoke experimental pilot. Local meanings only; no general recommendation implied.  
**Version:** 0.3  
**Updated:** 2026-11-25

## Grammar

Single Unicode code points represent phases, operators, components, or states. Adjacent tokens imply left-to-right succession. Structural operators preserve their defined semantics. The live signature carries codes; this ledger carries meanings. Memorization is unnecessary.

For live integrated-work signatures, square brackets group the subject components and their selected interpretive/method companions. Use the order **subject components → interpretive lens → method-source**. For example, `⊕[bhᛟdᵃ]` means integrated biology/history work read through the SAT/H(s)H lens, informed by the Dimensional Normalization paper, with archive-acquisition infrastructure active as a companion. The bracket group is a compact scope bundle, not a new branch or operator.

For branches, `⑂{cu}` is equivalent to `⑂{A: Credenza | B: Unicode notation}` when component codes are defined and left-to-right order is sufficient. Where additional ordering labels are needed, uppercase labels indicate branch/order positions and lowercase tokens identify components: `⑂{AcBu}`.

No undefined placeholders. A code may refer to a real, identifiable, populated, extensible collection.

## Phase codes

| Glyph | Code point | Canonical meaning | Class | Scope / constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ⌖ | U+2316 | Orient | Phase | Recover context and exact Tock/Tick position; consult the workshop ledger, protocol and code ledger; choose the authorized archive-search route before substantive archive retrieval |
| ◉ | U+25C9 | Focus / select Tock | Phase | Select and bound the substantial work unit |
| ⌕ | U+2315 | Investigate | Phase | Locate and examine sources or concepts |
| ⧖ | U+2996 | Geometrize | Phase | Construct the geometric/dimensional account |
| ⤳ | U+2933 | Connect | Phase | Follow relevant connections |
| ▣ | U+25A3 | Record | Phase | Preserve durable result |
| ✓ | U+2713 | Verify | Phase | Verify claims, original-source locators, archive query/scope/engine, repository commits and exclusions, run manifest/receipt, coverage limits, result and durable storage/readback |
| ⇢ | U+21E2 | Deliberate transition / next | Operator | Explicit decision/transition point; not ordinary succession |

### Archive retrieval and verification under ⌖ / ✓

> # **CRITICAL OPERATING INSTRUCTION — MYSEARCH / MERSEARCH**
>
> **THERE IS NO SEPARATE MERSEARCH OR MYSEARCH “TOOL EXPOSURE.” DO NOT LOOK FOR, REQUEST, OR EXPECT STANDALONE CONNECTOR TOOLS BY THOSE NAMES.**
>
> Mysearch and Mersearch are **bespoke search systems that exist in the archives**: their implementations, instructions, request schemas, bridge workflows, and result/receipt structures are archive-resident. Use them **through the connected archive connector**. The connector is the interface and transport/control layer: use its repository read, write, workflow, and artifact functions to inspect and invoke the archive-resident search interfaces. Where a bespoke search route exists for an archive task, it **replaces the connector's generic archive-search functions**; do not substitute generic search merely because Mysearch/Mersearch are not listed as separately exposed tools.
>
> For Mersearch, use the documented connector route (including the request-lane files and Actions bridge when appropriate), then inspect the request-specific manifest and receipt. Respect lane occupancy and publication/coverage limits. A compact receipt is not an exhaustive full-hit inventory. Mysearch's current operational/validation status must be checked in its archive records; the fact that it is not a standalone exposed tool says **nothing** about whether its archive-resident implementation or route exists.
>
> **Generic GitHub/code search is fallback only** when the documented bespoke archive route genuinely cannot be executed. If fallback is necessary, state the precise blocker and label the result as fallback, never as Mysearch or Mersearch.
>
- **Mysearch is the first-choice direct-Nathan archive-search route when operational and validated.** Its current repository status record still says `SCAFFOLD ONLY / NOT VALIDATED / NOT YET A PRODUCTION SEARCH SERVICE`; do not report a Mysearch execution or rely on it as an available production route until that status changes and the route is actually accessible.
- **Until Mysearch is operational, use Mersearch as the active archive-search standard**, pinned to stable Mersearch 1.0. Follow `Satobloc/HsH/WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_WORKER_START_HERE.md`; search all three permitted repositories together by default: `Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25`, `Satobloc/HsH`, and `Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES`. Preserve the distinct source status of HSH_RESOURCES as internal reference/toolkit material, not theory authority.
- Prefer the local pinned searcher for full, inspectable result sets. The GitHub Actions bridge's post-containment compact receipts are not exhaustive full-hit inventories. Never claim exhaustiveness from a compact receipt; report the searched roots, refs/SHAs, engine, query, exclusions, counts, receipt state and limitations.
- Use GitHub code search only as a documented fallback when Mysearch/Mersearch cannot actually be used. Label it as fallback search, not a Mysearch or Mersearch result, and disclose scope/coverage limitations. Do not silently substitute it.
- A search hit is not a source read. `✓` requires opening and inspecting the original matched source (or recording why it cannot be inspected), preserving exact locators and distinguishing searched, located, metadata-inventoried, read, and verified states.

## Defined collections

None registered yet. Add a collection only when it exists as an identifiable, populated list or registry. It may remain extensible.

## State and Tock tracking

Tock is the higher-level bounded work package; Tick is a subordinate operation or position marker within it. The Credenza routes and preserves Tocks; the Unicode string describes their internal Tick structure. Tock completion requires a durable result and recorded next cursor. The live signature is the Tick-level compact representation; the ledger stores full Tock status and history.


## Credenza register codes

| Glyph | Code point | Register | Class | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ≝ | U+225D | STATIC | Credenza register | Stable definitions and rules; definitions intended to persist across Tocks unless explicitly superseded. |
| ▶ | U+25B6 | NOW | Credenza register | Immediate active work; the current attention slot, not a separate phase. |
| ▷ | U+25B7 | NEXT | Credenza register | Ordered upcoming work not yet active. |
| ↩ | U+21A9 | RETURN | Credenza register | Re-entry instructions, exact resumption point and dependencies. |
| ⚑ | U+2691 | PIN | Credenza register | Ranked, mutable possibilities and deferred ideas; each pin has an ID, priority, capsule, state, trigger/return cue and pointer where warranted. |
| § | U+00A7 | SOURCES | Credenza register | Source identities, exact locators, provenance, reading state and access/coverage limits. |
| ⁇ | U+2047 | QUESTIONS | Credenza register | Unresolved questions, alternatives and discriminators. |
| ∴ | U+2234 | FINDINGS | Credenza register | Results, corrections and decisions with epistemic status. |
| ⚙ | U+2699 | METHODS | Credenza register | Tools, procedures, search routes, tests and quality controls. |
| ⋈ | U+22C8 | BRANCHES | Credenza register | Connected workstreams and their cross-links; does not imply equivalence. |
| ⏸ | U+23F8 | PARKED | Credenza register | Deferred work with a possible return trigger; not closed or superseded. |
| ⊘ | U+2298 | RETIRED | Credenza register | Superseded or closed work retained for history; not merely paused. |

**Use and separation rules**
- A glyph identifies a register, not a workflow action. It may head a ledger section or appear as a compact pointer in a Credenza capsule; it is not inserted into the Tock/Tick sequence merely because that register is being read or updated.
- NOW and NEXT are distinct: ▶ is active attention; ▷ is ordered but not yet active.
- PARKED and RETIRED are distinct: ⏸ preserves a deferred path with a possible return trigger; ⊘ preserves a superseded/closed path and its history.
- A PIN is mutable and ranked; it is not a commitment to execute. Do not create a blank/undefined pin or code placeholder.
- No register glyph supersedes @, and none changes the semantics of existing phase, operator, component or Tock codes.


## Change control

Never silently reassign a glyph. Add new codes with meanings, code points, class, scope, date/version, and syntax constraints. For changed meanings, retain a supersession record.

## Position marker

| Glyph | Code point | Canonical meaning | Class | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| @ | U+0040 | Current position marker | State marker | Prefixes the next uncompleted item in the active Tock/Tick sequence. It does not itself add a workflow operation. |

**Placement rule:** place `@` immediately before the next uncompleted token. The preceding tokens are completed; the following tokens remain. For a compound branch, place it before the next branch or operation to execute. If the next item is itself a compound structure, place it before that structure.
